prime_audit_s138.rubber_stamped: None adopted unverified — all 4 technically-specific Council challenges were re-checked on disk and all 4 were refuted. This is reflexion pattern #empirical-refutes-plausible-criticals firing for the 9th recorded time.
prime_audit_s138.self_indictment: The false consensus was partly MY fault. My Council prompt stated fact 12 (structuralSignature is size-only — true) WITHOUT stating that the differential rig actually compares hashWorldStateFull. Both models then reasoned correctly from an incomplete fact set and converged on the same wrong conclusion (abandon per-primitive HP). Lesson: a Council fed a partial fact set does not return 'uncertain' — it returns confident agreement on a wrong answer, which is far more dangerous than disagreement.
prime_audit_s138.runtime_verifiability: The field-level-guard claim is a DOCBLOCK CLAIM about a compile-time behaviour, not a verified fact. Static reading is not runtime validation. Mitigation promoted to execution step 1: actually add hp to Primitive, run tsc, and confirm it fails BY NAME before any design rests on it.
prime_audit_s138.synthesis_vs_r1: Materially better than R1. R1 (mine) said 'raze via the existing removal path'; synthesis established there is no such path and that extracting one shared helper is the de-risking step. That correction is the concrete value the deliberation produced.
